---
title: "1 Data and leakage"
---

Session 1 builds the data every later model learns from: a synthetic book of
{{< var score.n_applicants >}} small-business applicants, {{< var score.n_booked >}} of them
booked, generated by code you can read. Synthetic data is not a shortcut here. Because the
generator is known, every claim about the data can be checked against the process that made
it — which features cause default, which only look as if they do, and which columns a model
must never see. The session ends with a model that cheats, on purpose, so you recognise the
leak that actually ships.

## The videos

Seven chapters, one idea each, in session order.

{{< yt S1-c1 >}}

How the workshop works: an AI agent wrote the code under direction, and one command,
`python verify.py`, tells you where you are and that it works.

{{< yt S1-c2 >}}

The five milestones of the platform, and the one number they all rest on: the probability of
default.

{{< yt S1-c3 >}}

The finished platform before any theory: every applicant scored, a decision for each — the
portal approves {{< var adj.book.Approve.share >}} of them — and \${{< var pricing.mispriced_ead >}}
of booked exposure quoted below the hurdle. Session 3 takes these numbers apart, including
why that last one describes generated quotes rather than a pricing desk
([D6.7, finding 1](../mdd/pricing/limitations.qmd)).

{{< yt S1-c4 >}}

Why the data is synthetic, how the generator makes a default — a latent logit, noise, then a
coin flip — and the rule that some columns are never a model's input.

{{< yt S1-c5 >}}

Stage tags as save points, and the lab's two tracks: regenerate and audit the data by hand,
or hand a prompt card to an agent and grade its audit.

{{< yt S1-c6 >}}

A chart that lies: default rates by industry differ, and the difference means nothing. The
generator never uses industry; its information value is far below the conventional floor of
{{< var monitoring.iv_useless >}}. On the scorecard's own binning of the training applicants it
is {{< var score.iv.industry >}}; the video's figure comes from the notebook's per-industry
table on all applicants. An honest chart, an invented story.

{{< yt S1-c7 >}}

The leakage ladder. Four honest features score {{< var leakage.honest.auc >}}; add the
generator's true PD and the same model scores {{< var leakage.truepd.auc >}}; add the label
itself and it scores {{< var leakage.label.auc >}} — all on the same held-out applicants. The
last rung gets caught. The middle one looks like a good model, passes review, and ships.

- The Session 1 reading note,
  [`workshop/reading/S1-data-generation.pdf`](https://github.com/aayancheng/banking-analytics-workshop/blob/main/workshop/reading/S1-data-generation.pdf)

## Notebook and lab

- Notebook: [`notebooks/01_stage1_portfolio.ipynb`](https://github.com/aayancheng/banking-analytics-workshop/blob/main/notebooks/01_stage1_portfolio.ipynb)
  — open it in the Codespace and run it top to bottom. It audits the book, scans every safe
  column's information value, reads the deny-list, runs the leakage ladder and ends with a
  checkpoint card.
- Lab: [`workshop/labs/S1-lab.md`](https://github.com/aayancheng/banking-analytics-workshop/blob/main/workshop/labs/S1-lab.md)
  — generate and audit the portfolio, by hand or with an agent, then the leakage probe. Its
  own homework (bin one feature by hand, choose five features, seal the AUC you expect) is
  good preparation for Session 2.

The notebook and the lab run on `main`. To see the platform as it stood at the end of
Session 1, jump to its stage tag and restore the course material, which lives on `main` only:

```bash
git stash -u                  # park your own changes (git stash pop brings them back)
git checkout stage-1
git checkout main -- workshop notebooks wiki
python verify.py
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Look at `stage-0` before you restore anything
`stage-0` is the empty environment, and `git ls-files` there lists only a handful of files.
Restored files are staged, and staged files survive a later checkout, so if you run the
restore command first and then visit `stage-0`, `git ls-files` shows the restored folders as
well. Jump to `stage-0`, look, jump to `stage-1`, and only then restore.
:::

`git checkout main` brings you back to the finished platform. The homework assumes `main`.

## Check

```bash
python verify.py
```

The data line confirms the three committed files and their row counts: applicants, booked
accounts and the monthly panel. At `stage-1` that is the last check, and the final line reads
*Stage 1 verified*. On `main` the same line runs first, before every model's gate.

## Homework with an agent

Three exercises: ask an agent which columns leak and check its list against the deny-list;
build the ladder's middle rung and say why it cannot ship; and catch an agent that pins the
near-perfect AUC on the wrong column. Each has a self-check: [Session 1
homework](homework-s1.qmd).
